angular-momentum-conservation.name: Angular Momentum Conservation
angular-momentum-conservation.intro: Conserve angular momentum as the moment of inertia changes — compute the new angular velocity of a figure skater, collapsing system, or any spinning body when its mass distribution is altered.

angular-momentum.name: Angular Momentum
angular-momentum.intro: Compute the angular momentum of a rotating body from its moment of inertia and angular velocity, the rotational counterpart of linear momentum.

banked-curve.name: Banked Curve Speed
banked-curve.intro: Find the frictionless design speed for a banked curve from its radius and banking angle, where the horizontal component of the normal force supplies the centripetal force.

coefficient-restitution.name: Coefficient of Restitution
coefficient-restitution.intro: Determine the coefficient of restitution between two colliding objects from their approaching and separating velocities — a measure of how elastic (bouncy) the impact is.

elastic-collision-1d.name: 1D Elastic Collision
elastic-collision-1d.intro: Solve a one-dimensional perfectly elastic collision for the final velocities of both masses, where both momentum and kinetic energy are conserved.

hooke-force.name: Hooke's Law Force
hooke-force.intro: Apply Hooke's law to find the restoring force of a spring from its stiffness (spring constant) and displacement from equilibrium.

impulse.name: Impulse
impulse.intro: Calculate impulse as the product of force and time, equal to the change in linear momentum it produces.

inclined-plane-accel.name: Inclined Plane Acceleration
inclined-plane-accel.intro: Compute the acceleration of an object sliding down an inclined plane, accounting for gravity, the slope angle, and kinetic friction.

inelastic-collision.name: Inelastic Collision
inelastic-collision.intro: Find the common final velocity after a perfectly inelastic collision in which two objects stick together and kinetic energy is not conserved.

kinetic-friction.name: Kinetic Friction
kinetic-friction.intro: Compute the kinetic friction force opposing sliding motion from the coefficient of kinetic friction and the normal force.

moment-of-inertia-point.name: Point Mass Moment of Inertia
moment-of-inertia-point.intro: Calculate the moment of inertia of a point mass rotating about an axis at a given radius — the building block of rotational inertia.

momentum-conservation.name: Momentum Conservation
momentum-conservation.intro: Apply conservation of linear momentum to find the final velocity of a system when no external force acts, such as in a collision.

momentum.name: Momentum
momentum.intro: Compute linear momentum as the product of an object's mass and velocity — a vector quantity central to collision analysis.

period-pendulum.name: Pendulum Period
period-pendulum.intro: Find the period of a simple pendulum from its length and the local gravitational acceleration using the small-angle approximation.

power-force.name: Power from Force
power-force.intro: Calculate mechanical power delivered by a force moving an object at a given velocity (power = force × velocity).

power-rotational.name: Rotational Power
power-rotational.intro: Compute rotational power from torque and angular velocity (power = torque × angular speed) for motors, wheels, and shafts.

rotational-kinetic-energy.name: Rotational Kinetic Energy
rotational-kinetic-energy.intro: Find the kinetic energy stored in a rotating body from its moment of inertia and angular velocity.

spring-potential.name: Spring Potential Energy
spring-potential.intro: Compute the elastic potential energy stored in a compressed or stretched spring from its stiffness and displacement.

static-friction-max.name: Maximum Static Friction
static-friction-max.intro: Determine the maximum static friction force that can act before an object begins to slide, from the coefficient of static friction and the normal force.

terminal-velocity.name: Terminal Velocity
terminal-velocity.intro: Estimate the terminal (steady) falling speed of an object when aerodynamic drag balances its weight.

torque-force.name: Torque from Force
torque-force.intro: Calculate torque (moment of force) from the applied force, lever-arm length, and the angle between them.

weight-force.name: Weight Force
weight-force.intro: Compute an object's weight (gravitational force) from its mass and the local gravitational acceleration.

work-energy-theorem.name: Work-Energy Theorem
work-energy-theorem.intro: Apply the work-energy theorem: the net work done on an object equals its change in kinetic energy.
